statement: Samsung's example configuration pairs four zHBM stacks directly on top of a 1,200W accelerator, described as conserving roughly 100 watts while raising bandwidth
why: Power is the hard limit on how much compute a site can host, so energy saved per accelerator translates directly into more deployable capacity behind the same grid connection.

impact.mechanism: Cutting memory-interface power and improving bandwidth per accelerator raises usable compute per watt, easing the power ceiling that limits how many accelerators a site can deploy.

evidence.excerpt: significant bandwidth gains while conserving approximately 100 watts of energy

confidence.basis: Vendor-presented example configuration reported by a single secondary outlet; no performance-per-watt metric is stated, so no value is asserted.

dispersion: Stated for one described example configuration, not a measured product benchmark.
